props.gloss_en: the mishna: but if they sold a Torah scroll, they may not buy [other] scrolls [with the proceeds]
the question's first side: selling an old Torah scroll to buy a new one is forbidden, since it does not raise it [in sanctity]
the question's second side: it is permitted, since there is no further raising to be had

the baraita: a Torah scroll is rolled in the cloths of chumashin, chumashin in the cloths of Prophets and Writings; but not Prophets and Writings in the cloths of chumashin, nor chumashin in the cloths of a Torah scroll

the baraita: a Torah scroll is placed upon a Torah scroll, a Torah scroll upon chumashin, chumashin upon Prophets and Writings; but not Prophets and Writings upon chumashin, nor chumashin upon a Torah scroll
placing is different, for it cannot be otherwise -- so it is permitted
for if you do not say so, how could we furl [a scroll]? one sheet rests upon another! rather, since it cannot be otherwise, it is permitted

there [RSbG's prohibition] is on account of negligence
R' Meir: one sells a Torah scroll only to study Torah and to marry a woman
perhaps study is different, for study leads to action
a woman too: 'He did not create it a waste; He formed it to be inhabited' (Isaiah 45:18)
the baraita: a person may not sell a Torah scroll even though he does not need it
further, RSbG: even if he has nothing to eat and sold a Torah scroll or his daughter, he never sees a sign of blessing
